## Libraries

```{r libraries r}

library(qualtRics)
library(tidyverse)
library(janitor) 
library(stringr)
library(apollo) # for analysis
library(readxl) # for loading design
library(here)   # file paths relative to the project root (.Rproj)
```

## Load Datasets & Design

```{r load data & design}

# Qualtrics exports from July 31, 2026 (see data/README.md).
# Labels = "choice text" export, values = "numeric values" export.
qt_labels <- read_survey(here("data", "qualtrics_labels_2026-07-31.csv"))

qt_values <- read_survey(here("data", "qualtrics_values_2026-07-31.csv"))

# Experimental design workbook (committed at the repo root)
design_path <- here("SCORCH DCE Experimental Design Positly.xlsx")

design <- read_excel(design_path, sheet = "Design | Choice Tasks") |> clean_names()

# all model output (Apollo files + results tables) is written here
output_dir <- here("output")
dir.create(output_dir, showWarnings = FALSE)

# to maintain original data, create duplicate dataframes to work in from this point forward
df.labs <- qt_labels
df.vals <- qt_values
```

```{r recode & clean df.vals only}
# ! is used to exclude columns 
df.vals <- df.vals |> 
  mutate(across(where(is.numeric) 
                & !matches("^[ab][1-9]$")
                & !c(age, positly_age, household, household_u18, zipcode, duration_in_seconds, progress, q_recaptcha_score, signature_size, practice_question),factor)) 

# in qualtrics, a1 had different answer choice lvls (2/4) then the rest of the choice tasks (1/2). Recode a1 to match the rest.
df.vals <- df.vals |>
  mutate(a1 = case_when(a1 == 2 ~ 1, a1 == 4 ~ 2, TRUE ~ a1))
```

## Data-Quality Flags

Documented exclusion rules (see `docs/data-quality.md`). Respondents are only
**flagged** here. The headline model keeps everyone; a sensitivity model in the
model chunk re-estimates without the flagged respondents.

1. **Bot risk:** reCAPTCHA score below 0.5 (Google's usual threshold).
2. **Straight-lining:** chose the same side (all Park A or all Park B) in every choice task.
3. **Failed attention check:** `QC_agree` answered with anything other than "Agree".
   The check was only *shown* to block-2 respondents (Qualtrics survey-flow problem), so
   block-1 respondents can't be screened on this rule. This can't be fixed after the fact.
4. **Speeder:** total survey time below one third of the sample median.

```{r quality flags}

choice_cols <- str_subset(names(df.vals), "^[ab][1-9]$")

quality_flags <- df.vals |>
  select(response_id, q_recaptcha_score, duration_in_seconds, all_of(choice_cols)) |>
  left_join(df.labs |> select(response_id, qc_agree_label = qc_agree),
            by = "response_id") |>
  mutate(
    block           = if_else(rowSums(!is.na(pick(matches("^a[1-9]$")))) > 0, 1, 2),
    n_tasks         = rowSums(!is.na(pick(all_of(choice_cols)))),
    n_chose_A       = rowSums(pick(all_of(choice_cols)) == 1, na.rm = TRUE),
    attention_shown = !is.na(qc_agree_label),
    flag_recaptcha  = !is.na(q_recaptcha_score) & q_recaptcha_score < 0.5,
    flag_straightline = n_chose_A == 0 | n_chose_A == n_tasks,
    flag_attention  = attention_shown & qc_agree_label != "Agree",
    flag_speeder    = duration_in_seconds < median(duration_in_seconds) / 3,
    exclude_quality = flag_recaptcha | flag_straightline | flag_attention | flag_speeder
  ) |>
  select(response_id, block, n_tasks, n_chose_A, q_recaptcha_score,
         duration_in_seconds, qc_agree_label, attention_shown, starts_with("flag_"),
         exclude_quality)

# The attention check was not shown evenly: almost only block 2 saw it
quality_flags |> count(block, attention_shown)

# Speeder cut-off (seconds)
median(quality_flags$duration_in_seconds) / 3

# How many respondents each rule flags, and in total
quality_flags |>
  summarise(across(c(starts_with("flag_"), exclude_quality), sum))

# Respondents dropped in the quality sensitivity model
quality_flags |> filter(exclude_quality)

quality_exclude <- quality_flags |> filter(exclude_quality) |> pull(response_id)

write_csv(quality_flags, file.path(output_dir, "quality_flags.csv"))
```

## Reformat `df.vals`

```{r long reformat}

# create a new dataframe to store the reformation
survey_long <- df.vals |>
  select(response_id, matches("^[ab][1-9]$")) |>
  pivot_longer( #reshapes data to long format
    cols = matches("^[ab][1-9]$"),
    names_to = c("block", "choice_situation"),
    names_pattern = "([ab])(\\d+)",
    values_to = "choice") |>
  mutate(
    choice_situation = as.integer(choice_situation),
    block = case_when(block == "a" ~ 1, block == "b" ~ 2)) |>
  filter(!is.na(choice))

# recode survey_long's choice_situation to match the designs continuous numbering
survey_long <- survey_long |>
  mutate(choice_situation = if_else(block == 2, choice_situation + 9L, choice_situation))

#inspect and verify design date 
excel_sheets(design_path)
dim(design)
names(design)

# code to check that the choice_situation numbering matches the design
survey_long |> distinct(block, choice_situation) |> arrange(block, choice_situation)
design |> distinct(block, choice_situation) |> arrange(block, choice_situation)
```

## Join `survey_long`, `design`, and demographic data together

```{r join}

# first, create a new dataframe to store the joining of survey_long & design
dce_data <- survey_long |>
  left_join(design, by = c("block", "choice_situation"))

# second, create another dataframe that has specific demographic data pulled from df.vals, excluding demographic data that is irrelevant to analysis 
dce.demo <- df.vals |>
  select(-matches("^[ab][1-9]$"), -matches("_text$"), -practice_question,
         -start_date, -end_date, -progress, -duration_in_seconds, -finished, 
         -recorded_date, -distribution_channel, -user_language, -q_recaptcha_score, 
         -consent, -qc_agree, -comments, -adult, -south_az,
         -starts_with("positly"), -starts_with("signature"))

# third, recode T/F columns to 1/0, respectively
dce.demo <- dce.demo |> 
  mutate(across(where(is.logical), as.integer))

# lastly, create analysis ready dataset
final_data <- dce_data |> 
  left_join(dce.demo, by = "response_id") |> 
  mutate(avail_1 = 1, avail_2 = 1)

# quality check
dim(final_data)

sum(is.na(final_data$response_id))

table(final_data$block)

table(final_data$choice)

# confirm that every one of 756 choices matched its inteded experimental design
sum(is.na(dce_data$alt1_proximity))

# CHECK FOR ALTERNATIVE A CHOICE PATTERN

# Count how many times each participant selected Alternative A
a_choice_count <- final_data |>
  group_by(response_id) |>
  summarise(
    times_chose_A = sum(choice == 1),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

# Count how many participants selected Alternative A
# 0 through 9 times across their 9 choice tasks
# (0 = always chose B, 9 = always chose A; both are straight-lining)
a_choice_summary <- a_choice_count |>
  count(times_chose_A, name = "number_of_participants") |>
  complete(
    times_chose_A = 0:9,
    fill = list(number_of_participants = 0)
  )

a_choice_summary
```

```{r model}


# SET UP APOLLO CHOICE MODEL


# Initialize Apollo
apollo_initialise()

# Use original choice-task dataset for Apollo MNL
database <- final_data

# Add new variable long_term_az
database <- database |>
  mutate(
    long_term_az = if_else(yrs_az == 6, 1, 0)
  )

# Region from the self-reported ZIP code (first three digits).
# The screener only asked "Are you currently living in Southern Arizona?",
# and many Phoenix-area residents answered "Yes" (issue #2).
database <- database |>
  mutate(
    zip3 = str_sub(str_trim(as.character(zipcode)), 1, 3),
    zip_region = case_when(
      zip3 %in% c("856", "857")        ~ "Tucson / Southern AZ (856-857)",
      zip3 %in% c("850", "852", "853") ~ "Phoenix metro (850, 852-853)",
      zip3 == "851"                    ~ "Pinal County (851)",
      TRUE                             ~ "Other / missing"
    ),
    tucson_zip = as.integer(zip3 %in% c("856", "857"))
  )

# Respondents by ZIP region
database |>
  distinct(response_id, zip_region) |>
  count(zip_region)

# WHICH SAMPLE IS THE HEADLINE?
# "all"        = everyone who said they live in Southern Arizona (current results)
# "tucson_zip" = only respondents with a Tucson / Southern AZ ZIP (856-857)
# Every model below uses `database`; the region comparison always uses
# `database_all`. This is a framing decision, see issue #2.
analysis_sample <- "all"

database_all <- database

if (analysis_sample == "tucson_zip") {
  database <- database |> filter(tucson_zip == 1)
}

# Convert DCE attribute levels to integers
database <- database |>
  mutate(
    across(
      c(
        alt1_proximity, alt1_amenities, alt1_plant,
        alt1_safety, alt1_shade, alt1_accessibility,
        alt2_proximity, alt2_amenities, alt2_plant,
        alt2_safety, alt2_shade, alt2_accessibility
      ),
      as.integer
    )
  )

# Verify that each DCE attribute is coded using three levels
sort(unique(database$alt1_proximity))
sort(unique(database$alt1_amenities))
sort(unique(database$alt1_plant))
sort(unique(database$alt1_safety))
sort(unique(database$alt1_shade))
sort(unique(database$alt1_accessibility))

# Define Apollo model settings
# Each participant completed multiple DCE choice tasks
apollo_control <- list(
  modelName       = "MNL_DCE",
  modelDescr      = "MNL model of greenspace preferences",
  indivID         = "response_id",
  outputDirectory = output_dir
)

# Check analysis dataset
dim(database)
table(database$choice)

# Load attribute definitions from the experimental design
attribute_levels <- read_excel(design_path, sheet = "Attributes")

attribute_levels



# DEFINE MODEL PARAMETERS


# Starting values for the ASC and attribute-level coefficients
# A starting value of 0 does not mean the coefficient is fixed at 0

apollo_beta <- c(
  
  # Alternative-specific constant for Alternative A
  # Alternative B is the reference
  asc_A = 0,
  
  # Proximity
  b_proximity_1 = 0,
  b_proximity_2 = 0,
  b_proximity_3 = 0,
  
  # Amenities
  b_amenities_1 = 0,
  b_amenities_2 = 0,
  b_amenities_3 = 0,
  
  # Plant type
  b_plant_1 = 0,
  b_plant_2 = 0,
  b_plant_3 = 0,
  
  # Interaction: Plant type x Arizona residency
  b_plant_1_az = 0,
  b_plant_3_az = 0,
  
  # Safety
  b_safety_1 = 0,
  b_safety_2 = 0,
  b_safety_3 = 0,
  
  # Shade
  b_shade_1 = 0,
  b_shade_2 = 0,
  b_shade_3 = 0,
  
  # Accessibility
  b_accessibility_1 = 0,
  b_accessibility_2 = 0,
  b_accessibility_3 = 0
)

# Set one level of each attribute as the reference category
#
# References:
# Proximity: level 3 = 1 mile
# Amenities: level 3 = no additional amenities
# Plant: level 2 = mix of native and non-native plants
# Safety: level 1 = no safety features
# Shade: level 3 = no shade
# Accessibility: level 3 = no paths/no accessibility routes

apollo_fixed <- c(
  "b_proximity_3",
  "b_amenities_3",
  "b_plant_2",
  "b_safety_1",
  "b_shade_3",
  "b_accessibility_3"
)

# Validate the database and model settings
apollo_inputs <- apollo_validateInputs()


# ================================================================
# DEFINE MODEL AND LIKELIHOOD FUNCTION
# ================================================================

# Define the MNL probability function
apollo_probabilities <- function(
  apollo_beta,
  apollo_inputs,
  functionality = "estimate"
) {
  
  # Make model parameters and database variables available
  # within the probability function
  apollo_attach(apollo_beta, apollo_inputs)
  on.exit(apollo_detach(apollo_beta, apollo_inputs))
  
  # Create list of probabilities
  P <- list()
  
  # Define utilities for the two park alternatives
  V <- list()
  
  # Alternative A / Park 1
  # Includes the ASC for Alternative A
  V[["park1"]] <-
    asc_A +
    b_proximity_1     * (alt1_proximity == 1) +
    b_proximity_2     * (alt1_proximity == 2) +
    b_proximity_3     * (alt1_proximity == 3) +
    b_amenities_1     * (alt1_amenities == 1) +
    b_amenities_2     * (alt1_amenities == 2) +
    b_amenities_3     * (alt1_amenities == 3) +
    b_plant_1         * (alt1_plant == 1) +
    b_plant_2         * (alt1_plant == 2) +
    b_plant_3         * (alt1_plant == 3) +
    b_plant_1_az * (alt1_plant == 1) * long_term_az +
    b_plant_3_az * (alt1_plant == 3) * long_term_az +
    b_safety_1        * (alt1_safety == 1) +
    b_safety_2        * (alt1_safety == 2) +
    b_safety_3        * (alt1_safety == 3) +
    b_shade_1         * (alt1_shade == 1) +
    b_shade_2         * (alt1_shade == 2) +
    b_shade_3         * (alt1_shade == 3) +
    b_accessibility_1 * (alt1_accessibility == 1) +
    b_accessibility_2 * (alt1_accessibility == 2) +
    b_accessibility_3 * (alt1_accessibility == 3)
  
  # Alternative B / Park 2
  # Alternative B is the reference for the ASC
  V[["park2"]] <-
    b_proximity_1     * (alt2_proximity == 1) +
    b_proximity_2     * (alt2_proximity == 2) +
    b_proximity_3     * (alt2_proximity == 3) +
    b_amenities_1     * (alt2_amenities == 1) +
    b_amenities_2     * (alt2_amenities == 2) +
    b_amenities_3     * (alt2_amenities == 3) +
    b_plant_1         * (alt2_plant == 1) +
    b_plant_2         * (alt2_plant == 2) +
    b_plant_3         * (alt2_plant == 3) +
    b_plant_1_az * (alt2_plant == 1) * long_term_az +
    b_plant_3_az * (alt2_plant == 3) * long_term_az +
    b_safety_1        * (alt2_safety == 1) +
    b_safety_2        * (alt2_safety == 2) +
    b_safety_3        * (alt2_safety == 3) +
    b_shade_1         * (alt2_shade == 1) +
    b_shade_2         * (alt2_shade == 2) +
    b_shade_3         * (alt2_shade == 3) +
    b_accessibility_1 * (alt2_accessibility == 1) +
    b_accessibility_2 * (alt2_accessibility == 2) +
    b_accessibility_3 * (alt2_accessibility == 3)
  
  # Connect the two utility functions to the observed
  # choice and availability variables
  mnl_settings <- list(
    alternatives = c(park1 = 1, park2 = 2),
    avail        = list(
      park1 = avail_1,
      park2 = avail_2
    ),
    choiceVar = choice,
    utilities = V
  )
  
  # Calculate MNL choice probabilities
  P[["model"]] <- apollo_mnl(
    mnl_settings,
    functionality
  )
  
  # Account for repeated choice tasks completed by each respondent
  P <- apollo_panelProd(
    P,
    apollo_inputs,
    functionality
  )
  
  # Prepare and return probabilities for model estimation
  P <- apollo_prepareProb(
    P,
    apollo_inputs,
    functionality
  )
  
  return(P)
}


# HELPERS FOR ESTIMATING AND REPORTING MODELS

# Interaction parameters (plant type x 10+ years in AZ).
# Fixing them at 0 gives the model without the interaction.
interaction_pars <- c("b_plant_1_az", "b_plant_3_az")
main_fixed <- c(apollo_fixed, interaction_pars)

# Estimate the MNL on a given sample. By default the interaction is left out
# (the headline specification); pass fixed = apollo_fixed to include it.
# Uses the same apollo_beta / apollo_probabilities defined above.
fit_mnl <- function(data, model_name, model_descr, fixed = main_fixed) {
  control <- modifyList(apollo_control,
                        list(modelName = model_name, modelDescr = model_descr))
  inputs <- apollo_validateInputs(
    apollo_beta    = apollo_beta,
    apollo_fixed   = fixed,
    database       = as.data.frame(data),
    apollo_control = control
  )
  fit <- apollo_estimate(apollo_beta, fixed, apollo_probabilities, inputs)
  apollo_modelOutput(fit)
  apollo_saveOutput(fit)
  fit
}

# One row per parameter: estimate, robust SE, robust p-value.
# Matches by parameter name, so it does not depend on the order of apollo_beta.
tidy_mnl <- function(fit) {
  rse <- fit$robse
  if (is.null(names(rse))) names(rse) <- names(fit$estimate)
  tibble(
    parameter = names(fit$estimate),
    estimate  = unname(fit$estimate),
    robust_se = unname(rse[names(fit$estimate)])
  ) |>
    mutate(robust_t = estimate / robust_se,
           p_value  = 2 * pnorm(-abs(robust_t)))
}


# ESTIMATE MODELS

# Headline model: no plant x residency interaction.
# The interaction is not supported by the data (see the LR test below), and
# with it in the model the plant "main effects" only describe respondents
# with under 10 years in Arizona.
model <- fit_mnl(
  database,
  model_name  = "MNL_DCE_main",
  model_descr = "MNL of greenspace preferences (headline, no interaction)"
)

# Secondary model: plant type x 10+ years in Arizona
model_interaction <- fit_mnl(
  database,
  model_name  = "MNL_DCE_plant_x_AZ",
  model_descr = "MNL with plant type x 10+ years in AZ interaction",
  fixed       = apollo_fixed
)

# Likelihood-ratio test: does the interaction improve fit?
apollo_lrTest(model, model_interaction)

lr_interaction <- tibble(
  LL_main        = model$maximum,
  LL_interaction = model_interaction$maximum,
  chi_sq         = 2 * (LL_interaction - LL_main),
  df             = model_interaction$numParams - model$numParams,
  p_value        = pchisq(chi_sq, df, lower.tail = FALSE)
)

lr_interaction

write_csv(lr_interaction, file.path(output_dir, "lr_test_interaction.csv"))


# SENSITIVITY: DROP RESPONDENTS FLAGGED BY THE DATA-QUALITY RULES

model_quality <- fit_mnl(
  database |> filter(!response_id %in% quality_exclude),
  model_name  = "MNL_DCE_quality",
  model_descr = "MNL (no interaction) excluding respondents flagged by data-quality rules"
)

quality_comparison <- tidy_mnl(model) |>
  select(parameter, all_est = estimate, all_p = p_value) |>
  left_join(tidy_mnl(model_quality) |>
              select(parameter, excl_est = estimate, excl_p = p_value),
            by = "parameter") |>
  filter(!is.na(all_p)) |>
  mutate(across(ends_with("_est"), \(x) round(x, 3)),
         across(ends_with("_p"), \(x) signif(x, 2)))

quality_comparison

write_csv(quality_comparison, file.path(output_dir, "sensitivity_quality_exclusions.csv"))


# SAMPLE GEOGRAPHY: TUCSON-ZIP SUBSAMPLE VS. EVERYONE ELSE (issue #2)

model_tucson <- fit_mnl(
  database_all |> filter(tucson_zip == 1),
  model_name  = "MNL_DCE_tucson_zip",
  model_descr = "MNL (no interaction), respondents with 856/857 ZIP codes"
)

model_non_tucson <- fit_mnl(
  database_all |> filter(tucson_zip == 0),
  model_name  = "MNL_DCE_non_tucson_zip",
  model_descr = "MNL (no interaction), respondents without 856/857 ZIP codes"
)

model_all <- if (analysis_sample == "all") model else fit_mnl(
  database_all,
  model_name  = "MNL_DCE_all",
  model_descr = "MNL (no interaction), full sample"
)

# Pooling test: do Tucson-ZIP and other respondents share the same
# preference parameters? (Likelihood ratio, pooled vs. separate models.
# Ignores possible scale differences between groups; with n = 36 vs. 48
# it has little power, so read the estimates side by side as well.)
lr_region <- tibble(
  LL_pooled   = model_all$maximum,
  LL_separate = model_tucson$maximum + model_non_tucson$maximum,
  chi_sq      = 2 * (LL_separate - LL_pooled),
  df          = model_tucson$numParams + model_non_tucson$numParams - model_all$numParams,
  p_value     = pchisq(chi_sq, df, lower.tail = FALSE)
)

lr_region

region_comparison <- tidy_mnl(model_all) |>
  select(parameter, all_est = estimate, all_p = p_value) |>
  left_join(tidy_mnl(model_tucson) |>
              select(parameter, tucson_est = estimate, tucson_p = p_value),
            by = "parameter") |>
  left_join(tidy_mnl(model_non_tucson) |>
              select(parameter, other_est = estimate, other_p = p_value),
            by = "parameter") |>
  filter(!is.na(all_p)) |>
  mutate(across(ends_with("_est"), \(x) round(x, 3)),
         across(ends_with("_p"), \(x) signif(x, 2)))

region_comparison

write_csv(region_comparison, file.path(output_dir, "sensitivity_region_tucson_zip.csv"))
write_csv(lr_region, file.path(output_dir, "lr_test_region_pooling.csv"))


# CREATE MNL RESULTS TABLES

# Labels for every parameter, looked up by name
param_labels <- tribble(
  ~parameter,          ~attribute,                       ~level,
  "asc_A",             "Alternative-specific constant",  "Alternative A vs. B",
  "b_proximity_1",     "Proximity",                      ">4 miles",
  "b_proximity_2",     "Proximity",                      "2-4 miles",
  "b_proximity_3",     "Proximity",                      "1 mile",
  "b_amenities_1",     "Amenities",                      "Gathering areas",
  "b_amenities_2",     "Amenities",                      "Nature play",
  "b_amenities_3",     "Amenities",                      "No additional amenities",
  "b_plant_1",         "Plant type",                     "Mostly native plants",
  "b_plant_2",         "Plant type",                     "Mix of native and non-native plants",
  "b_plant_3",         "Plant type",                     "Mostly non-native plants",
  "b_plant_1_az",      "Plant type x Arizona residency", "Mostly native plants: difference for 10+ yrs in AZ",
  "b_plant_3_az",      "Plant type x Arizona residency", "Mostly non-native plants: difference for 10+ yrs in AZ",
  "b_safety_1",        "Safety",                         "No safety features",
  "b_safety_2",        "Safety",                         "Lighting",
  "b_safety_3",        "Safety",                         "Patrol",
  "b_shade_1",         "Shade",                          "Shade from ramada",
  "b_shade_2",         "Shade",                          "Shade from a tree",
  "b_shade_3",         "Shade",                          "No shade",
  "b_accessibility_1", "Accessibility",                  "Mostly paved paths and accessible amenities",
  "b_accessibility_2", "Accessibility",                  "Some natural paths and limited accessibility routes",
  "b_accessibility_3", "Accessibility",                  "No paths and no accessibility routes"
)

# Plant effect for long-term residents in the interaction model:
# main effect + interaction, with a delta-method robust SE
long_term_plant_effects <- function(fit) {
  V <- fit$robvarcov
  map_dfr(c("1", "3"), function(k) {
    main <- paste0("b_plant_", k)
    int  <- paste0("b_plant_", k, "_az")
    tibble(
      parameter = paste0(main, "_longterm"),
      estimate  = fit$estimate[[main]] + fit$estimate[[int]],
      robust_se = sqrt(V[main, main] + V[int, int] + 2 * V[main, int])
    )
  }) |>
    mutate(
      attribute = "Plant type",
      level = c("Mostly native plants (10+ yrs in AZ)",
                "Mostly non-native plants (10+ yrs in AZ)"),
      robust_t = estimate / robust_se,
      p_value  = 2 * pnorm(-abs(robust_t))
    )
}

format_results <- function(tab) {
  tab |>
    mutate(reference = case_when(
      parameter == "asc_A" ~ "B is reference",
      is.na(robust_se)     ~ "Reference",
      TRUE                 ~ ""
    )) |>
    transmute(
      Attribute   = attribute,
      Level       = level,
      Estimate    = round(estimate, 3),
      `Robust SE` = round(robust_se, 3),
      `Robust t`  = round(robust_t, 2),
      `p-value`   = case_when(
        is.na(p_value)  ~ "",
        p_value < .001  ~ "< .001",
        TRUE            ~ sprintf("%.3f", p_value)
      ),
      Reference   = reference
    )
}

# Headline table (no interaction): plant effects apply to the whole sample
final_results <- tidy_mnl(model) |>
  filter(!parameter %in% interaction_pars) |>
  left_join(param_labels, by = "parameter") |>
  format_results()

final_results

# Interaction table: with the interaction in the model, b_plant_1 / b_plant_3
# are the effects for respondents with UNDER 10 years in Arizona. The
# long-term-resident effects (main + interaction) are added as extra rows.
results_interaction <- tidy_mnl(model_interaction) |>
  left_join(param_labels, by = "parameter") |>
  mutate(level = if_else(parameter %in% c("b_plant_1", "b_plant_3"),
                         paste0(level, " (under 10 yrs in AZ)"),
                         level))

plant_rows <- which(results_interaction$parameter == "b_plant_3_az")

final_results_interaction <- bind_rows(
  results_interaction[seq_len(plant_rows), ],
  long_term_plant_effects(model_interaction),
  results_interaction[-seq_len(plant_rows), ]
) |>
  format_results()

final_results_interaction

# Save the reporting tables next to the Apollo output files
write_csv(final_results, file.path(output_dir, "mnl_results_table.csv"))
write_csv(final_results_interaction,
          file.path(output_dir, "mnl_results_table_plant_x_AZ.csv"))
```
